panel.summary: `touchUpdatedAt`'s monotonic guard (`where: { updatedAt: { lt: at } }`) is untested — the idempotency/out-of-order property the code and webhook rely on is unverified
panel.evidence: document.service.ts adds `touchUpdatedAt` whose whole point (per its docstring) is that it only moves time forward and no-ops on missing rows. document.service.spec.ts (new in this diff) tests only `updateDocument`; it never constructs a service with an `updateMany` mock. The controller spec mocks `touchUpdatedAt` away entirely (yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:9-12), so no test would catch dropping the `lt` filter and letting an out-of-order/duplicate webhook move `updatedAt` backwards.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts::`touchupdatedat`'s monotonic guard (`where: { updatedat: { lt: at } }`) is untested — the idempotency/out-of-order property the code and webhook rely on is unverified

coderabbit.detail: **Document the empty-PATCH exception.** This says every metadata update bumps `updatedAt`, but the implementation intentionally skips the bump for empty PATCH requests. Qualify this as “every non-empty metadata update” to keep the design contract accurate.
